quote: I will mount a long wind some day and break the heavy waves / And set my cloudy sail straight and bridge the deep, deep sea.
source: Li Bai, The Hard Road, closing couplet, The Jade Mountain, p. 70 (trans. Witter Bynner, 1929)

evidence.where: scan-backed Wikisource page transcription of The Jade Mountain, read as raw wikitext; the couplet closes the poem and the printed folio at the foot of the page is 70
evidence.edition: The Jade Mountain: A Chinese Anthology, trans. Witter Bynner from the texts of Kiang Kang-hu (Alfred A. Knopf, 1929)
evidence.locator: printed p. 70, THE HARD ROAD (Written to Music), final two lines, after the refrain Journeying is hard; scan sequence 114

reason: The couplet is verbatim and does close the poem, directly after the refrain the proposal quoted. A page was added: 70. The 1929 running head prints the poet as Li Po, which is the same man as Li Bai, so the modern byline stands.
